title: Binyamin the Shepherd
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Berakhot 40b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.40b.6): he ate bread and said, “Blessed is the Master of this bread,” and Rav said, “He has fulfilled his obligation.” In [Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.6.2.3), a certain Persian asked Rav about this. Hyman concludes that undoubtedly Binyamin the Shepherd was from the land of Persia.[^2]

notes.text: כרך ריפתא here means that he ate bread, as the William Davidson English Berakhot 40b also renders the accompanying Aramaic. The conclusion that Binyamin was Persian is Hyman’s inference from the separate Jerusalem Talmud account, not a new identity binding.

The linked Bavli gives the full blessing “Blessed is the Merciful One, Master of this bread.” In the linked Yerushalmi, an unnamed Persian asks Rav about a similar blessing. From the parallel, Hyman concludes that Binyamin was undoubtedly from Persia.
